trust_decision.summary: Unconfirmed (fix diff is empty). Most plausible: tenant-admin JS rule-node scripts are evaluated into one shared Nashorn sandbox/engine global, so the global objects and prototypes one script modifies (JSON, Object.prototype) persist into every other script's execution; the remote js-executor instead creates a fresh vm context for each invoke.

landing_point.why: The advisory mentions code execution in a sandboxed context; the local Nashorn sandbox eval is the obvious sandbox for tenant JS scripts on the Java side. msa/js-executor/api/jsExecutor.ts:67 is the Node-side alternative.

fix_sites.entry_point: unknown: fix.diff contains only a merge header (fix.diff:1-2) with no hunks

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: msa/js-executor/api/jsExecutor.ts:52-81 (remote Node vm executor, separate package/language from the Nashorn path); unverified whether the published fix touched it

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Node executor creates a fresh context for each invoke and already builds args from sandbox-realm prototypes (msa/js-executor/api/jsExecutor.ts:67-74), so a solver can argue it is already hardened. Its non-sandbox mode is documented as dangerous by design (msa/js-executor/api/jsExecutor.ts:28-32).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The wrapper relies on global JSON.parse/JSON.stringify, and rule scripts legitimately add properties to msg/metadata objects and declare top-level helper functions in the wrapper. Freezing or disabling these globals wholesale would break normal transform scripts.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: REST POST /api/ruleChain/testScript evaluates a tenant JS script in the same JsInvokeService as rule nodes
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a test/debug endpoint, not the rule engine

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Rule nodes (transform, filter, switch, log, alarm, generator) create JS engines via TbContext.createScriptEngine into the same shared engine
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same sink as the landing point; unknown whether the fix closes it centrally

O8b_injection_room.sibling: doRelease evals into the same shared global, so a reset/isolation step that only covers eval and invoke could miss it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Release is a separate lifecycle path that also evaluates code in the same shared global

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the non-sandbox createFunction/invokeFunction path shares the host realm
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a second executor mode in the same class, and a maintainer would plausibly harden only the sandbox branch

O9_family: prototype pollution / shared-global state in a script sandbox (CWE-1321)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Blacklist '__proto__'/'prototype' tokens in JsValidator.validate instead of isolating each script's global state

out_of_scope_notes: argNames from the testScript request body are passed through String.format into the JS wrapper without validation (application/src/main/java/org/thingsboard/server/controller/RuleChainController.java:358-373, common/script/script-api/src/main/java/org/thingsboard/script/api/RuleNodeScriptFactory.java:47-49); this is wrapper code injection, a separate concern.
